name: Nguyen Minh Khoa
title: AI Engineer & Researcher
summary: I’m Khoa Nguyen, an AI engineer and Research Assistant at AiTA Lab, FPT University.

My recent work includes handwritten mathematical expression recognition and text-to-molecule generation. I have worked across data preparation, model experiments, and inference integration, with a preference for research that can be checked in working software.

I’m now focusing on AI for manufacturing, especially visual systems that must cope with limited data and changing operating conditions. I’m looking for work that gives equal weight to careful experiments and hands-on implementation.
I’m open to AI engineering, research engineering, and applied machine-learning collaborations.

experience.title: Research Assistant | AiTA Lab, FPT University
short: Co-authored two HMER papers at ICDAR and in the Journal of Information and Telecommunication, contributing masked-language pretraining and multi-task learning experiments.
First-authored LexiChem (APWeb-WAIM 2026): developed methods, ran ablations and presented the work in Da Nang. Co-first author of ChemAligner-T5 (ICCIES 2026).

full: First-authored LexiChem, accepted at APWeb-WAIM 2026, and presented it in Da Nang. Developed method ideas, ran experiments and ablations, wrote the Introduction and Results & Discussion, and co-wrote Methods.
Co-first-authored Mask CoMER (ICDAR 2025) and co-authored the MTL + CBARM journal paper, contributing pretraining and multi-task learning experiments for mathematical expression recognition.

projects.title: LexiChem | AI & Inference Contributor
projects.context: Completed capstone | Three-person team | Local application
short: Built the AI inference workflow so users can generate molecules from text, validate structures and revisit saved runs using FastAPI, Triton, RDKit and MongoDB.
Built a three-dataset training pipeline and ran ablations for the first-author APWeb-WAIM paper.
full: Built the AI path in a three-person capstone, bringing text-to-molecule models into an application where users generate, compare and inspect molecular candidates in 2D/3D.
Created training-ready SELFIES data from Mol-Instructions, L+M-24 and ChEBI-20 by validating structures, canonicalizing SMILES and removing duplicates with RDKit.
Developed shared-latent text/SELFIES alignment ideas and tested them through experiments and ablations, forming the research core of the first-author APWeb-WAIM paper.
Integrated FastAPI/Triton inference, RDKit structure checks and MongoDB storage into Experiments, connecting prompt entry to validated molecules and saved runs.
projects.stack: Python, PyTorch, Transformers, RDKit, SMILES/SELFIES, FastAPI, NVIDIA Triton, MongoDB
